intro: Searching for the best commercial conveyancer near you usually means you're dealing with a shop, office, industrial unit or investment property, and you want someone local who knows this kind of work well. Commercial conveyancing carries its own wrinkles — VAT, lease terms, wider due diligence — so finding the right person matters. We can introduce you to a suitable UK conveyancer who will quote you directly, with the price on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a commercial conveyancer usually need
need_lead: The situations behind this search tend to involve business premises rather than a home, and the details vary a lot from one deal to the next.
needs: You are buying or selling a shop, office or industrial unit and want a conveyancer who deals with commercial property rather than only residential homes.
You are taking on or granting a lease and need the terms examined carefully before you commit.
You want someone based near you who you can reach easily while the transaction runs.
You are weighing up several local firms and want to judge for yourself which one suits your deal.
You need help with the wider due diligence that commercial property involves, beyond what a residential purchase would need.
context_heading: Judging who is best for your commercial deal
context: No one can tell you in advance who is the best commercial conveyancer, and we won't claim that of anyone we introduce. What you can do is compare firms on how they handle commercial work: ask how they approach VAT on commercial property, how they examine lease terms, and what their due diligence covers beyond a standard residential purchase. Conveyancing in England and Wales is a reserved legal activity, carried out either by solicitors regulated by the SRA or by licensed conveyancers regulated by the Council for Licensed Conveyancers, and both must hold professional indemnity insurance and follow strict rules on handling client money.

Being near you is useful for a commercial deal, but check the practical points too. If you are borrowing to fund the purchase, many lenders only work with conveyancers on their panel, so confirm the firm is on your lender's panel before you instruct them. In Scotland, property transactions are handled by solicitors under Scottish law, so the position differs if your property is there.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say whether you are buying, selling, leasing or taking a lease of commercial premises.
Describe the type of property — for example a shop, office, industrial unit or investment property.
Mention where the property is located so we can look for someone near you.
Explain whether VAT is likely to be an issue on the transaction.
Note whether you are using a lender, so the panel point can be checked.
Include any deadlines or particular concerns you have about the lease terms or due diligence.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the commercial conveyancer
questions: How do you handle VAT on commercial property in a transaction like mine?
What does your due diligence cover that goes beyond a residential purchase?
How will you examine the lease terms and explain them to me?
Are you on my lender's panel, if I am borrowing to fund this purchase?
Who will handle my matter day to day, and how will you keep me updated?
What information and documents will you need from me to get started?

faqs.q: Can iComply tell me who the best commercial conveyancer is?
faqs.a: No — we don't rank or rate professionals, and we won't claim anyone is the best. We introduce you to a suitable UK conveyancer who quotes you directly, and you decide by comparing how they handle commercial work.

faqs.q: Why does commercial conveyancing cost more to look into than a home purchase?
faqs.a: Commercial property brings extra considerations such as VAT, lease terms and wider due diligence, so there is often more to examine. The conveyancer will quote you directly, price on application, once they understand your deal.

faqs.q: Do I need a conveyancer near me for a commercial purchase?
faqs.a: It is not a legal requirement to use someone local, but many people prefer a firm they can reach easily. Tell us where the property is and we will look for a suitable conveyancer near you.

faqs.q: Does it matter whether my conveyancer is a solicitor or a licensed conveyancer?
faqs.a: Both can carry out conveyancing in England and Wales — solicitors are regulated by the SRA and licensed conveyancers by the Council for Licensed Conveyancers. Either way they must hold professional indemnity insurance and follow strict rules on handling client money.

extra_heading: What happens once you instruct a commercial conveyancer
extra: Once you have chosen someone and told them about your deal, a commercial conveyancer usually starts by checking the title to the property and raising enquiries with the seller's side. They will also look at matters that rarely arise with a home purchase, such as whether VAT applies, what the lease says if there is one, and whether there are any restrictions on how the premises can be used.

You should expect to be asked for documents early on — the heads of terms if a lease is being negotiated, any planning or environmental information you hold, and details of your lender if you are borrowing. Because commercial due diligence is wider than residential, the enquiries stage often takes longer and raises more questions, so keep in touch with your conveyancer about anything that could affect your plans for the premises.

A useful first conversation is to ask how they will keep you informed and who your main point of contact will be. It also helps to ask what they need from you and by when, so you can gather paperwork without holding up the transaction. If a lease is involved, ask them to explain the repairing and insurance obligations clearly before you sign anything.

extra_faqs.q: Will a commercial conveyancer also advise me on the business side of the deal?
extra_faqs.a: Conveyancers deal with the legal side of the property — the title, the lease and the due diligence. They do not usually advise on whether the deal makes commercial sense for your business, so you may want separate advice on that.

extra_faqs.q: Can I use the same conveyancer for a commercial purchase and a related lease?
extra_faqs.a: Often the same firm can handle both parts if they are connected, but you should tell them about all the arrangements from the start. They will explain what they can and cannot act on for you, and quote you directly.

extra_faqs.q: What should I bring to a first meeting with a commercial conveyancer?
extra_faqs.a: Bring whatever you have about the property — the heads of terms, any draft lease, planning information and your lender's details if you are borrowing. The more they can see early, the clearer their quote and advice will be.
